ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee; close the dispute and inform the rider that the fee was validly charged under NS-4, with any further relief to be sought via a RydeHELP fee-waiver request under NS-7.
ruling.reasoning:
NS-0 routes the case by who cancelled: the system record shows cancelled_by = rider at 17:15:05, an instant booking, so the fee is governed by NS-4, not by the no-show clauses NS-1/NS-2 [F2][RD-2][NS-0]. The trace confirms this element (✓ cancelled_by = rider) [F2][NS-0].

NS-4 charges $6.61 where the rider cancels an instant booking more than 3 minutes after matching: acceptance was 17:12:00 and cancellation 17:15:05, i.e. 185 s = 3 min 5 s, which exceeds the 3-minute line [F2][NS-4]. The trace likewise finds this element satisfied (✓ 185 s after acceptance) [F2][NS-4]. The charge on record is exactly the published $6.61 with 1.0× surge — no unpublished or extra item appears, so FARE-1 is not engaged [F5][F6][FARE-1]. The only permitted outcomes given the trace are no_action or escalate; nothing in the record supports escalation [F2][NS-4].

NS-1/NS-2 do not apply on these facts. NS-1's arrival-and-wait test is the test a driver must meet when he cancels claiming the rider was a no-show; here the driver neither cancelled nor pressed "I'm Here", and the platform recorded no arrival (driver_arrived_at null, driver_pressed_here_at null) [F3][F4][NS-1]. Because no such claim was made, the failure of NS-1(i)–(iii) does not convert the rider's own cancellation into a refund — it simply means no no-show fee was ever chargeable against the rider on the driver's side [F3][F4][NS-1][NS-2]. NS-3 is also inapplicable: it governs a driver who cancels without a valid reason, and the driver did not cancel [F2][F10][NS-3].

The rider's stated ground — that the driver was still far away — does not create a refund as of right. The GPS record (closest approach 1725 m at 17:15:05, never within 200 m) and the driver's own message ("Coming, about 5 min" at 17:13) and statement ("cancelled while I was still on the way") show he had not arrived, but Ryde publishes no free-cancellation right for a driver running slower than the displayed ETA [F1][F8][F10][NS-4]. The rider's remedy is the NS-7 route: a fee-waiver request within 30 days, paid as a voucher if granted, and Ryde retains discretion over the outcome [NS-7]. Amount: no refund is computed because no refundable element is established; the $6.61 charge stands [F2][F5][NS-4].

SAFETY-1 screen: I read every chat message, the driver's statement and the complaint. Chat #1 "Are you near?" and Chat #2 "Coming, about 5 min" are ordinary coordination; the driver's statement "The rider cancelled while I was still on the way" and the rider's complaint about the fee contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][F10][F5][SAFE-1]. Safety finding: none.

EVIDENCE: the record settles every element this ruling needs — the cancelling party and the cancellation timestamp (system timeline), the fee amount (fare), the absence of any arrival confirmation (timeline), and a complete, fully timestamped chat (2 messages) [F2][F3][F4][F5][F9][NS-4][NS-0]. No gap that changes the outcome; evidence_status = sufficient.

rejected_claims.reason: NS-0 routes a rider-initiated cancellation of an instant booking to NS-4, not to NS-1/NS-2; NS-1(i) is unmet but no driver-side no-show claim was ever made, so its failure does not trigger an NS-2 refund [F2][F3][F4][NS-0][NS-1][NS-2].

The driver's distance from the pickup (1725 m, never within 200 m) defeats only an NS-1(ii) arrival element that was never asserted; it does not make the fee refundable when the rider is the cancelling party under NS-4 [F1][F2][NS-1][NS-4].

The absence of any recorded arrival (driver_arrived_at null) leaves NS-1(iii) unmet, but with no no-show claim by the driver this is irrelevant to chargeability, which rests on the rider's own cancellation [F2][F3][NS-1][NS-4].

The chat corroborates non-arrival but equally shows the rider cancelled 3 min 5 s after matching; NS-3 concerns a driver who cancels without valid reason and has no application to a rider cancellation [F2][F7][F8][NS-0][NS-3][NS-4].

The $6.61 is chargeable under NS-4 because the rider cancelled more than 3 minutes after matching; NS-7 governs only the form and timing of a payable refund, not whether one is owed [F2][F5][NS-4][NS-7].
The withdrawn traffic claim (mid-band speed on Sims Avenue East, no incidents, fair weather) does not affect the outcome, which is grounded in the rider's own NS-4 cancellation [F11][F12][F13][NS-4].

The driver's statement that the rider cancelled while he was still on the way confirms non-arrival but is not an admission of wrongdoing and does not make the fee refundable [F1][F2][F10][NS-4][NS-3].

Accepted as far as it goes, but the request to leave the fee in place is granted for the NS-4 reason, not for lack of any overcharge; no account flag arises because no RD-6 condition (upheld route deviation) is met [F5][F6][F14][F15][RD-6][FARE-1].
